name: NVIDIA Corporation
monetization: Sells AI accelerators, systems, and networking; increasingly also an investor in and financier of its own customer base.
description_md: NVIDIA designs GPUs and full-rack AI systems (Blackwell, Vera Rubin), networking (NVLink, Spectrum-X), and the CUDA software stack that together dominate AI training and inference compute. Data-center revenue is ~92% of total. Manufacturing is outsourced, principally to TSMC (wafers, CoWoS advanced packaging) with HBM memory from SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung.
ai_monetization_md: Direct hardware/systems sales to hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises, and sovereigns; software (AI Enterprise, DGX Cloud); and a growing investment portfolio (>$40B of equity commitments across the ecosystem in 2026 YTD) that critics argue partially funds its own demand. In Aug 2026 NVIDIA announced a >$500B financing coalition with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to fund customer purchases via compute-collateralized SPV bonds.
ai_strategy_md: Sell the full data-center stack rather than chips alone; lock in multi-year supply (≈60% of TSMC 2026 CoWoS capacity booked) and demand (Huang claims ~$1T revenue visibility through 2027); seed strategic customers and suppliers with equity (OpenAI $30B, xAI SPV, Intel $5B, Anthropic ≤$10B, Nokia, Nebius, Nscale, Naver, SSI); backstop customer financing where debt markets hesitate (proposed ~$250B OpenAI guarantee, in talks).
risk_notes_md: Customer concentration: four direct customers were 61% of revenue in Q1 FY27 (each >10%). Circularity: equity investments and financing structures touch a material share of its demand (see flows). China: zero data-center compute revenue assumed in guidance after export bans; a 15%-of-China-revenue license arrangement with the US government applied to prior H20 sales.
